caseno: Civil Petition for Special Leave to Appeal No. 93 of 1992
lawyer: Md. Sultan Ahmad, Advocate instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-On-Record ------for the Respondent
parties:
Mohammad Abdul Quddus ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mohammad Mustafa Hossain ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
M.H. Rahman, J: The plaintiff respondent preferred an appeal against the dismissal of his suit by the trial Court. On his prayer the appellate Court permitted him by an order dated 13th February, 1990, to withdraw the appeal as well as the suit, but not set the decree of the trial court. 

 2. The High Court Division, by the impugned order, refused to interfere in the matter, after holding that there was not only formal defect in the plaint, but there was also sufficient ground for permitting the plaintiff to withdraw the suit. It was further observed that appellate Court's omission to state expressly that the decree of the trial court was set aside "cannot be termed as an error of law. Because, as a matter of fact, the ultimate effect of withdrawal is certainly to do away with the entire proceedings of the suit and the appeal as if there had not been any such proceeding at all."
